name: Global X U.S. Infrastructure Development ETF
structure: Long PAVE shares + Jul 17 '26 $55 protective put (~$1.25)
thesis: Position for a broader shift toward rebuilding the physical economy as infrastructure, supply chains, transportation, energy systems, and strategic manufacturing become central to economic statecraft.
notes: Effective cost basis ~$58.49; floor $55.00 through Jul 17 '26 expiry; no covered call — full upside retained.

name: Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF
structure: Long XLV shares + Aug '26 collar (buy $145 put ~$1.90 / sell $165 call ~$1.24, ~$0.66 net debit)
thesis: Position for a rotation back into healthcare as crowded momentum and AI-related trades become vulnerable, while healthcare begins showing signs of accumulation and relative improvement.
notes: Effective cost basis ~$153.51; floor $145, upside capped $165 — approaching but not yet at the cap.

name: Invesco DB Agriculture Fund
structure: Bull call spread: long Jan 15 '27 $27 call ($1.70) / short Jan 15 '27 $30 call ($0.80), $0.90 net debit
thesis: Building on Brent Johnson's delayed food-supply thesis; position for agricultural stress emerging into Q4 2026 and Q1 2027.
notes: Better than 2:1 payoff ($2.10 max) if DBA ≥ $30 at Jan 15 '27 expiry; max loss is the $0.90 debit; long-dated structure gives the thesis time to play out.

name: United States 12 Month Natural Gas Fund
structure: Long UNL — Delta-One, no options overlay
thesis: AI power-demand bottleneck / natural gas as bridge fuel. Chosen over UNG to avoid front-month contango roll drag.
notes: Simple buy-and-hold equity position, laddered exposure across the 12-month futures curve.

name: Valero Energy
structure: Bull call spread: long Aug 21 $270 call ($15.00) / short Aug 21 $300 call ($5.75), $9.25 net debit
thesis: Refiners directly benefit from strong crack spreads while crude itself remains sloppy/oversupplied — leaning into refiners rather than picking a bottom in crude.
notes: Max payoff $20.75 (>2:1) if VLO ≥ $300 at Aug 21 expiry; max loss is the $9.25 debit.

name: Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF
structure: Long XLE shares + Aug 21 '26 50/65 collar (buy $50 put ~$0.30 / sell $65 call ~$0.20, ~$0.10 net debit)
thesis: Energy offers a way to stay constructive on equities without adding to already-crowded AI/tech exposure.
notes: Hedge floor ~$50, upside capped ~$65; short call sits above 52-week high.

name: Cheniere Energy
structure: Long LNG shares + $240 protective put, 36 DTE (~$4.55)
thesis: US LNG buildout tied to energy security and AI/data-center power demand.
notes: Put hedge ~1.8% cost; technical failure/floor at $240.

name: SPDR Gold Shares
structure: Long GLD + put-spread collar: long Sep 18 $370 put ($8.50) / short Sep 18 $350 put ($3.50) / short Sep 18 $415 call ($3.25), $1.75 net cost
thesis: Gold, oil, and rates rising together may signal the market pricing in longer-term inflationary/fiscal consequences of prolonged war spending.
notes: Approaching the $415 call cap; upside above $415 is forfeited under this structure. Downside protection band ($370–$350) is well out of the money.

name: iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF
structure: Bear put spread: long Aug 21 $82 put ($0.80) / short Aug 21 $80 put ($0.30), $0.50 net debit
thesis: Inflation remains too persistent for the bond market to relax — either the Fed tightens or long yields do it for them.
notes: Max profit $1.50 (3-to-1) if TLT closes at/below $80 at expiration.

name: Global X Robotics & Artificial Intelligence ETF
structure: Long BOTZ shares + Aug $37 protective put (~$0.60, 16 DTE)
thesis: Rotation out of crowded chip/infrastructure names into robotics & automation, a segment that already underwent a meaningful valuation reset.
notes: Put expires ~Aug 22, 2026; stop/exit logic keyed to $37.

name: SPDR Gold Shares
structure: Bull call spread: long Oct 16 '26 $410 call ($15.00) / short Oct 16 '26 $450 call ($4.50), $10.50 net debit
thesis: Building on Michael Howell's structurally bullish but tactically-inflecting gold view — using gold's steep right-tail volatility skew to finance a defined-risk bullish structure targeting the next leg higher.
notes: Near 3-to-1 payoff (risk ~$10.50 to make ~$30) if GLD is at/above $450 at Oct 16 '26 expiry.

name: iShares Bitcoin Trust
structure: Deep in-the-money call (stock-replacement): long Jan 15 '27 $32 call for $8.75 (≈$7.00 intrinsic, ≈$1.75 time value)
thesis: Building on Darius Dale's fiscal-dominance/financial-repression framework — scarce assets benefit structurally from continued debasement, with Bitcoin as a direct expression of that thesis.
notes: Capital-efficient stock-replacement alternative to owning IBIT outright; max loss = premium paid; delta rises toward 1 as IBIT rallies.

name: NVIDIA Corp.
structure: Long at-the-money call: buy Jan 15 '27 $225 call for ~$21.60 (IV ~38%, near 1-yr lows)
thesis: Building on Matt Barrie's accelerating-agentic-AI thesis: structurally bullish AI, but not a clean tactical entry, so buy cheap long-dated optionality instead of the shares.
notes: Defined risk (max loss = premium), positive vega if NVDA corrects into the midterms, open-ended upside if semis re-accelerate. 128 days to expiry at entry.

name: iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF
structure: Long strangle: buy Jan 15 '27 $85 call (~$0.82) + $77 put (~$0.97) = $1.79 debit
thesis: Building on Harley Bassman's trust/fiscal-credibility and mortgage-convexity concerns: own bond volatility in either direction rather than picking a direction on yields.
notes: NON-DIRECTIONAL: changePct (underlying move) is not meaningful here; the trade profits from a large move either way (~7% to break even at expiry) or a rise in implied vol. Final P&L uses the real two-leg payoff.

name: United States Oil Fund
structure: Bull call spread: long Jan 15 '27 $150 call ($15.50) / short $180 call ($7.25), $8.25 net debit
thesis: Building on Michael Every's view that low oil prices don't mean geopolitical risk has gone; another pipeline/export-route disruption could quickly reverse the relief move.
notes: ~3:1 reward/risk; $180 on USO is roughly crude at ~$120/bbl. Max loss = premium if USO <= $150 at expiry.

name: S&P 500 (SPX put, tracked via SPY proxy)
structure: Long OTM put: buy Jan 14 '27 SPX 7430 put for ~136 index points (~30 delta, ~1.8% of notional), SPX ~7,653
thesis: Building on David Rosenberg's view that the energy shock damages growth more than it creates lasting inflation; cheap 3-month vol ahead of a consequential Q4 (earnings, two FOMCs, midterms, Hormuz).
notes: Actual trade is on the SPX index, which the price source doesn't carry, so it's tracked via SPY. Legs are scaled to SPY terms by the entry-day SPY/SPX ratio (0.09983): strike ~741.73, premium ~13.58. Expiry breakeven ~7,294 SPX (~4.7% below reference).

name: Canadian dollar (CAD futures put)
structure: Long put on Canadian dollar futures: buy Nov 6 '26 70.00 US-cent put for 22 pips (~$220/contract), CAD ~70.37
thesis: Building on Brent Johnson's dollar-milkshake view and his specific preference for USD over CAD: the dollar keeps attracting capital as higher rates hit more vulnerable economies harder.
notes: Prices are in US cents per CAD. Daily closes are CAD/USD spot (x100), backfilled manually because the price pipeline doesn't track FX and skips expired trades. Futures traded slightly above spot (carry). RESULT: expired Nov 6 with spot ~70.78, above the 70 strike, so the put expired worthless (-22 pips, -100% of premium).

name: Centrus Energy Corp.
structure: Cash-secured short LEAPS put: sell Jan 21 '28 $70 put for ~$10.25 ($1,025/contract), strike ~43% below spot
thesis: Building on Yasir Arafat's point that reactor mass-production only scales if enriched-fuel supply scales with it; Centrus is the US domestic enrichment play. Get paid to commit to owning it far below today's price.
notes: netCostBasis is set to the $70 strike (the cash-secured obligation), so final P&L % = return on capital at risk: +14.6% if it expires above $70. If assigned, effective cost is ~$59.75/share. Max profit = premium.

name: JPMorgan Chase (long leg of JPM/DB pair)
structure: Equal-dollar pair: long JPM ~$334.58 / short Deutsche Bank (DB) ~$32.39 (~10.3 DB shares short per JPM share); optional hedge: long Apr 16 '27 DB $36 call ~$2.00 per 100 DB short
thesis: Building on Louis-Vincent Gave's France thesis: French fiscal/energy stress could spread through Europe's banks. European financials (EUFN +57% since the Liberation Day lows) have more than doubled US financials (XLF +27%), so there's room for that leadership to reverse.
notes: PAIR TRADE: the site tracks only the JPM leg (single-ticker limitation). Pair P&L = JPM % change minus DB % change; DB entry $32.39 (tracked manually in the local Trade Tracker). The DB call overlay caps the DB-leg loss at ~$5.61/share.

name: Capital One Financial
structure: Bear put spread: long Jan 15 '27 $200 put / short $175 put, ~$5.96 net debit (alt: long $200 put outright ~$7.95)
thesis: Building on Luke Gromen's AI-unemployment consumer-credit thesis: if AI erodes workers' earning power, consumer lenders' credit quality deteriorates. COF (cards + auto) has been in a downtrend since January and is pivoting at its 50-day.
notes: Max profit ~$19.04 vs. $5.96 risked (~3.2:1). Individual leg premiums are inferred: $200 put ~$7.95 (quoted), so the $175 put is ~$1.99.

name: Marathon Petroleum Corp.
structure: Bull call spread: long Dec 18 '26 $390 call (~$30) / short $450 call (~$10), $20 net debit
thesis: Building on Michael Every's view that markets are too quick to price lasting energy relief: continued refinery attacks keep refining capacity tight and margins strong. MPC fell ~23% in 16 days, an overshoot.
notes: 2:1 reward/risk; breakeven $410 (~4.4% above reference); tactical mean-reversion trade with 43 days to expiry.

name: Sprott Physical Uranium Trust
structure: Bull call spread on U.UN (Montreal options, CAD): long Jan 15 '27 C$25 call (~C$2.50) / short C$28 call (~C$0.90), C$1.60 net debit
thesis: Uranium's supply deficit is independent of the AI cycle, yet the trust is being sold with the AI basket and trades at a deep discount to NAV (working NAV ~C$31.50). A narrowing of the discount to 5-10% (~C$28.35) reaches the upper strike without uranium rising; higher uranium prices are a second route.
notes: PROXY: the trade is on the TSX listing U.UN in CAD (ref C$26.60), which Alpha Vantage doesn't carry, so the site tracks the US OTC line SRUUF (USD close $17.85 on 2026-11-12). Legs and net debit are scaled by the entry-day SRUUF/U.UN ratio (17.85/26.60 = 0.6711), which also embeds USD/CAD; original CAD legs: C$25/C$28 strikes, C$2.50/C$0.90 premiums, C$1.60 debit. Breakeven C$26.60 (the reference), max profit C$1.40 at >=C$28 (~0.9:1).
